pillars.title: Series Room Generation
pillars.header: Build a Universe, Not a Clip
pillars.body: Describe your series or YouTube channel once, and SceneFlow builds the whole world — storyline, cast, and an unlimited episode slate — with a Shared Reference Library that keeps every episode on-brand.

steps.title: Start with your concept
steps.description: Drop in a concept or a detailed description of your series or YouTube channel. SceneFlow turns it into a structured, production-ready foundation — no prompt engineering required.
steps.imagePlaceholder: New series intake — concept or channel description

steps.title: Review the SceneFlow baseline
steps.description: SceneFlow returns a professional baseline scored by Audience Resonance Analysis. Read or listen to the narrated overview, then steer it with your own direction.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Series baseline — Audience Resonance score and narrated overview

steps.title: Create unlimited episodes
steps.description: Spin up as many episodes as your story needs. Each one inherits your series DNA, so the cast, tone, and world stay consistent from episode one to the season finale.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Episode slate — unlimited episodes generated from the series arc

steps.title: Review the Reference Library
steps.description: Browse the shared Reference Library — characters, voices, wardrobe, locations, and props — created and maintained through Production Stage and reused across every episode.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Shared Reference Library — characters, voices, locations, props

steps.title: Direct the Intelligent Assistant Writer
steps.description: Reshape the series or any episode by speaking or typing your direction. The Intelligent Assistant Writer rewrites professional copy instantly — no blank page, no prompt engineering.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Intelligent Assistant Writer — voice or text direction on series and episodes

steps.title: Start production in one click
steps.description: When an episode feels right, start its production with a single click and flow straight into the guided Production Stage pipeline.
steps.imagePlaceholder: One-click start production on a selected episode

pillars.title: Blueprint Room
pillars.body: Blueprint Room is your deep film treatment — synopsis, beats, characters, tone, and style — pre-scored by Audience Resonance Analysis so you approve a story that lands before a single frame renders.

steps.title: Review the baseline Blueprint
steps.description: Open a professional baseline Blueprint with Audience Resonance Analysis built in. Read or listen to the narrated overview to hear exactly why it works.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Baseline Blueprint — treatment with Audience Resonance score

steps.title: Direct the Intelligent Assistant Writer
steps.description: Refine the synopsis, beats, characters, and more by speaking or typing your direction. The Intelligent Assistant Writer revises the treatment instantly — no prompt engineering.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Intelligent Assistant Writer — editing synopsis, beats, and characters

steps.title: Review the Reasoning
steps.description: Open the Reasoning section for a creative explanation of the current Blueprint — the story logic behind every beat and character choice.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Reasoning panel — creative explanation of the Blueprint

steps.title: Start production when ready
steps.description: Once the story sings, start production — and the entire pipeline inherits your approved creative DNA with no drift.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Open Production Stage — readiness gate from an approved blueprint

pillars.title: Production Stage
pillars.body: Production Stage runs concurrent, multi-engine generation — script, audio, frames, and video — with the Intelligent Assistant Director, the Screening Room, and multilanguage streams carrying you from approved script to a published 4K master.

steps.title: Review the baseline script
steps.description: Start from a professional baseline script with Audience Resonance Analysis. Read or listen to the narrated analysis to know what lands before you spend a credit.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Baseline script — Audience Resonance analysis and narrated overview

steps.title: Optimize scene by scene
steps.description: Use the Intelligent Assistant Writer to optimize the script scene by scene — tighten dialogue, reshape beats, and apply one-click improvements by voice or text.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Intelligent Assistant Writer — scene-by-scene script optimization

steps.title: Build the Reference Library
steps.description: Create or update the Reference Library with scripted, custom, or uploaded characters, voices, wardrobes, locations, and props. Edit reference images directly — no "slot machine" regenerations.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Reference Library — characters, voices, wardrobe, locations, props

steps.title: Generate audio
steps.description: Generate dialogue, narration, SFX, and music with Run All Agents across all scenes, Audio Agent per scene, or shot by shot — native-quality voiceover in 70+ languages.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Audio Agent — all scenes, single scene, or shot by shot

steps.title: Generate and edit frames
steps.description: Generate shot frames with Run All Agents, Stills Agent per scene, or shot by shot, then edit any frame with the Intelligent Assistant Director (IAD) — just describe the change.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Shot frames with Intelligent Assistant Director edits

steps.title: Review the animatic
steps.description: Play the full animatic — frames, dialogue, SFX, and music — in the interactive Screening Room, and share a link for feedback without exporting a file.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Screening Room — interactive animatic review and sharing

steps.title: Generate video
steps.description: Turn approved frames into motion with Video Agent per scene or shot by shot. Retake any shot with the Intelligent Assistant Director — no endless slot-machine regenerations.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Video Agent generation with IAD retakes

steps.title: Edit in the Mixer
steps.description: Polish every scene in the Mixer — captions, trims, dubbing, overlays, and audio balance — brand-safe finishing without leaving the studio.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Mixer — captions, trim, dubbing, and audio controls

steps.title: Render and review scenes
steps.description: Render your scenes, then review and share them through the Screening Room to lock approval before final assembly.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Rendered scenes reviewed and shared in the Screening Room

steps.title: Generate multilanguage streams
steps.description: Spin up dubbed or lip-synced language streams from the same approved cut — reach 70+ markets without re-shooting a single frame.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Multilanguage streams — dubbed and lip-sync per locale

steps.title: Render final and publish
steps.description: Render the final production into a master and publish — auto-generated thumbnails, titles, and descriptions ready for your YouTube channel and beyond.
steps.imagePlaceholder: Final render and one-click publish to YouTube

keyFeatures.title: From the idea to the master.
keyFeatures.subtitle: Series Room → Blueprint Room → Production Stage → Screening Room.
keyFeatures.landingUiLanguagesLabel: Produce and dub in 44 languages. This site is available in these 39:

rooms.label: Series Room
rooms.promise: Lock the franchise once. Season arcs, cast, tone, and world rules carry into every episode, and a single film can skip this room.

features.title: Season universe
features.description: Define the franchise once. Season arcs, recurring cast, tone, and world rules live on the series, and every new episode inherits them instead of starting from a blank page. A single film can skip this room and open in the Blueprint Room.

learnMore.problem: A new episode that starts from a blank page forgets the cast, the tone, and the rules of the world.
learnMore.solution: Season universe stores arcs, recurring cast, tone, and world rules on the series so every episode inherits them.
learnMore.outcome: A single film can skip Series Room. A season keeps one franchise definition for every episode.

features.title: Episode handoff
features.description: Each episode outline, synopsis, and story beats sync into that episode’s Blueprint Room and Production Stage. Episode 12 still knows the cast, the world, and what already happened.
features.screenshot: Episode handoff into Blueprint and Production

learnMore.problem: Later episodes lose the thread when the outline, the synopsis, and the beats live somewhere else.
learnMore.solution: Episode handoff syncs that episode’s outline, synopsis, and story beats into its Blueprint Room and Production Stage.
learnMore.outcome: Episode 12 still knows the cast, the world, and what already happened.

features.title: Reshape · with Direction
features.description: The series edit dialog. Speak or type what should change — a more sympathetic antagonist, a new subplot, a different climax — and optionally focus the edit on plot, characters, episode content, tone, or setting. The revision is targeted. Unrelated parts of the storyline stay put, and you apply the change yourself.

learnMore.problem: A broad rewrite of the series can change plot, cast, and setting you meant to keep.
learnMore.solution: Reshape · with Direction takes a spoken or typed note and can focus the edit on plot, characters, episode content, tone, or setting. You preview it and apply it yourself.
learnMore.outcome: Unrelated parts of the storyline stay put. Nothing is rewritten until you accept the change.

features.title: Direct this episode
features.description: The series-episode edit. On one episode, dictate the change (raise the stakes, deepen the B-story) and apply it to that episode only. The rest of the season is left alone.

learnMore.problem: A note about one episode should not rewrite the rest of the season.
learnMore.solution: Direct this episode takes the change you dictate and applies it to that episode only, after you accept it.
learnMore.outcome: The rest of the season is left alone.

rooms.label: Blueprint Room
rooms.promise: A sentence or a brief becomes the treatment and the only beat sheet. Score it for the audience you named, then share it before anyone spends on pictures.

features.title: Treatment and beat sheet
features.description: A sentence or a full brief becomes the film treatment: motivations, characters, art direction, and a beat sheet. Beats exist only here. Production Stage turns each beat into a chapter; it does not invent a second beat sheet.

learnMore.problem: A second beat sheet in production splits the story from the treatment you already locked.
learnMore.solution: Treatment and beat sheet turns a sentence or a full brief into motivations, characters, art direction, and the only beat sheet.
learnMore.outcome: Production Stage turns each beat into a chapter. It does not invent another beat sheet.

features.title: Audience Resonance
features.description: Score concept, tone, characters, and beats against the audience you named, before anyone spends on pictures. You see the score and the recommendations, then decide what to revise.

learnMore.problem: Picture spend starts before you know whether the concept, tone, characters, or beats fit the audience.
learnMore.solution: Audience Resonance scores those parts against the audience you named and shows the recommendations.
learnMore.outcome: You decide what to revise before anyone spends on pictures.

features.title: Co-Director · Blueprint
features.description: The Blueprint edit dialog (Co-Director · Blueprint). Describe the change in plain words. Preview the rewrite, keep the parts you want, and apply it without throwing away the visual foundation already locked in the treatment.

learnMore.problem: A rewrite of the treatment can throw away art direction you already locked.
learnMore.solution: Co-Director · Blueprint takes the change in plain words, shows a preview, and lets you keep the parts you want.
learnMore.outcome: You apply the rewrite without throwing away the visual foundation. Nothing changes until you accept it.

features.title: Stakeholder review
features.description: Share the treatment as a read-and-listen link. Collaborators hear the narration and see the same board you do. Their notes come back as guided revision, not a new document in another tool.

learnMore.problem: Feedback that arrives as a separate document has to be retyped into the treatment.
learnMore.solution: Stakeholder review shares a read-and-listen link. Collaborators hear the narration and see the same board.
learnMore.outcome: Their notes come back as guided revision on the board you already have.

rooms.label: Production Stage
rooms.promise: Write the script, spend with your own keys and a budget, generate with locked references, mix the scene, and deploy languages, 4K, versions, and trailers.

features.title: Bring Your Own Key
features.description: Connect your own image and video provider keys. Generation runs on your account, with your rates, while the guided studio — agents, references, Mixer, and Screening Room — stays in place. You are not choosing between cost control and the pipeline.

learnMore.problem: Controlling model cost often means leaving the guided studio for a raw provider account.
learnMore.solution: Bring Your Own Key connects your image and video provider keys so generation runs on your account, at your rates.
learnMore.outcome: Agents, references, the Mixer, and Screening Room stay in place. Cost control and the pipeline are the same studio.

features.title: Budget Manager
features.description: Set a credit budget for the project and watch it move as audio, stills, and clips are generated. Guidance points at the cheap cuts first: draft frames, fewer generations, add-on credits when you need more runway. You see the overrun before the render, not after.

learnMore.problem: Credit overruns show up after the render, when the runway is already gone.
learnMore.solution: Budget Manager tracks a project credit budget as audio, stills, and clips are generated, and points at draft frames, fewer generations, or add-on credits first.
learnMore.outcome: You see the overrun before the render.

features.title: Writer's Room
features.description: The production script, scene by scene, in the language of the story. Dialogue, pacing, and tone are revised here, with Audience Resonance scoring beside the page, before a frame is spent.

learnMore.problem: Dialogue, pacing, and tone get revised after frames are already paid for.
learnMore.solution: Writer's Room holds the production script scene by scene, with Audience Resonance scoring beside the page.
learnMore.outcome: You revise the page before a frame is spent.

features.title: Script Audience Resonance
features.description: A test-audience read of the script: overview, analysis, and scene notes, with section scores and recommendations. You choose which notes to act on. Nothing is rewritten until you open a director dialog and apply it.

learnMore.problem: A test-audience note that rewrites the script on its own can change scenes you meant to keep.
learnMore.solution: Script Audience Resonance shows an overview, analysis, scene notes, section scores, and recommendations. You choose which notes to act on.
learnMore.outcome: Nothing is rewritten until you open a director dialog and apply it.

features.title: Scene Director
features.description: The script-scene dialog, titled Scene Director · Scene N, opened from a scene’s Audience Resonance recommendations (Direct Scene, or Direct Scene & Apply). You direct that scene, preview the changes, and select which changes to keep. The rest of the script stays as you left it.

learnMore.problem: A note about one scene should not rewrite the rest of the script.
learnMore.solution: Scene Director opens from a scene’s Audience Resonance recommendations — Direct Scene, or Direct Scene & Apply. You direct that scene, preview the changes, and select which to keep.
learnMore.outcome: The rest of the script stays as you left it. The scene changes only when you apply them.

features.title: Script Director
features.description: The whole-script dialog. Revise the full script from Audience Resonance recommendations, preview the new draft, and apply it only when you accept it. Use this when the note is about the film, and Scene Director when the note is about one scene.

learnMore.problem: A note about the whole film is the wrong job for a single-scene edit, and a whole-script rewrite should not apply itself.
learnMore.solution: Script Director revises the full script from Audience Resonance recommendations and shows the new draft first.
learnMore.outcome: You apply it only when you accept it. Use Scene Director when the note is about one scene.

features.title: Reference Library
features.description: Lock cast, wardrobe, voices, locations, and props to the production’s art style. Every still and clip asks this library for the same faces and places, so a later scene does not recast the lead.

learnMore.problem: A later scene recasts the lead when faces, wardrobe, and places are not locked to the art style.
learnMore.solution: Reference Library locks cast, wardrobe, voices, locations, and props. Every still and clip asks that library for the same faces and places.
learnMore.outcome: The lead stays the lead from scene to scene.

features.title: Production Agents
features.description: Audio, Stills, and Video agents read the locked direction, attach the right references, and build the scene in the background. You iterate in draft, then render motion. Standard clips use Veo 3.1, which delivers 4K. Longer Omni preview clips are a separate model; their 4K option is not on yet. You direct and approve; the agents prompt and generate.

learnMore.problem: Prompting each still and clip by hand drops the locked direction and the references that belong on the shot.
learnMore.solution: Audio, Stills, and Video agents read the locked direction, attach the right references, and build the scene in the background. Standard clips use Veo 3.1, which delivers 4K. Longer Omni preview clips are a separate model, and their 4K option is not on yet.
learnMore.outcome: You iterate in draft, then render motion. You direct and approve; the agents prompt and generate.

features.title: Direct Shot
features.description: The shot dialog, titled Direct Shot · Scene N · Shot N. You direct the shot in plain language, preview the direction, and save it. The preview spells out the shot you are approving: frozen moment and action, camera (shot, angle, movement, transition), blocking, emotion, gaze, lighting, props, and audio. Connected references — cast, locations, and objects — stay attached to that shot. Saving updates the still prompt and the clip prompt together. You can also steer a clip with the video-direction chips: Camera move, Action shots, Hold the start frame, Match the end frame, and Keep faces.
features.screenshot: Direct Shot with camera and references

learnMore.problem: A shot direction that hides the camera, the blocking, or the references makes you approve a prompt you cannot see.
learnMore.solution: Direct Shot · Scene N · Shot N takes plain language, then previews frozen moment and action, camera (shot, angle, movement, transition), blocking, emotion, gaze, lighting, props, and audio. Connected cast, locations, and objects stay attached. Saving updates the still prompt and the clip prompt together.
learnMore.outcome: You can also steer a clip with Camera move, Action shots, Hold the start frame, Match the end frame, and Keep faces. The shot is saved when you save it.

features.title: Pre-Vis before motion
features.description: A Ken Burns animatic with dialogue, score, and sound effects, built from the approved stills. Watch the scene, change direction with Direct Shot if it is wrong, and only then render motion.

learnMore.problem: Motion renders get spent on a scene whose staging is still wrong.
learnMore.solution: Pre-Vis before motion builds a Ken Burns animatic with dialogue, score, and sound effects from the approved stills.
learnMore.outcome: Watch the scene, change it with Direct Shot if it is wrong, and only then render motion.

features.title: Mixer
features.description: The scene finish inside Production Stage. Balance dialogue, narration, score, and effects, include or drop individual shots, and render the scene with its audio. Language Streams are prepared from this same Mixer, and the rendered scene is what Screening Room plays.

learnMore.problem: Dialogue, narration, score, and effects get finished in a separate editor, then the picture and the dub drift apart.
learnMore.solution: Mixer balances those tracks, includes or drops individual shots, and renders the scene with its audio. Language Streams are prepared from this same Mixer.
learnMore.outcome: Screening Room plays the rendered scene.

features.title: Language Streams
features.description: A language version of the scene, not a new production. Gemini TTS speaks the dub in 44 languages. For a non-English stream you can keep the original ambience and turn on Kling lip-sync so the dubbed dialogue is performed on the picture, or ship the dub on the existing shots. Add a language from the Mixer and generate that stream without rebuilding the cut.
features.screenshot: Language Streams with the lip-sync switch

learnMore.problem: A dub that requires a new production rebuilds the cut for every language.
learnMore.solution: Language Streams is a language version of the scene. Gemini TTS speaks the dub in 44 languages. For a non-English stream you can keep the original ambience and turn on Kling lip-sync, or ship the dub on the existing shots.
learnMore.outcome: Add a language from the Mixer and generate that stream without rebuilding the cut.

features.title: Delivery resolution
features.description: Veo 3.1 renders the master in 4K. That is a native render, not an upscale. Choose the delivery tier when you stitch the language master; optional Topaz upscaling still sharpens a cut when those credentials are connected. Omni stays in preview. Its 4K control is expected in January 2027.

learnMore.problem: An upscale is not the same as a master rendered at 4K, and a preview model is not the model that delivers it.
learnMore.solution: Veo 3.1 renders the master in 4K as a native render. Choose the delivery tier when you stitch the language master. Optional Topaz upscaling still sharpens a cut when those credentials are connected.
learnMore.outcome: Omni stays in preview. Its 4K control is expected in January 2027.

features.title: Version control
features.description: Every take of a stream is kept. Compare them, pin the one people liked, and come back to it after later edits. A new generation does not erase the previous cut.

learnMore.problem: A new generation replaces the take people already liked.
learnMore.solution: Version control keeps every take of a stream so you can compare them and pin one.
learnMore.outcome: You can come back to that take after later edits. A new generation does not erase the previous cut.

features.title: Promotion trailers
features.description: Promotion trailers weave a 30–60 second 9:16 promo from the strongest beats. It is ready for Shorts, Reels, and TikTok, and it is cut from the same locked timeline as the master.

learnMore.problem: A promo cut in another tool drifts away from the locked timeline.
learnMore.solution: Promotion trailers weave a 30–60 second 9:16 promo from the strongest beats.
learnMore.outcome: The trailer is ready for Shorts, Reels, and TikTok, and it is cut from the same locked timeline as the master.

rooms.label: Screening Room
rooms.promise: Watch the cut the Mixer rendered, review it on one link, and publish a scene, a chapter, the master, or a promo when that piece is ready.

features.title: One player
features.description: Switch among Pre-Vis, scenes, chapters, the master, and promo. Pick a Language Stream and hear that dub, including a lip-synced version when you generated one. The player is the same cut the Mixer rendered.

learnMore.problem: Pre-Vis, scenes, chapters, the master, the promo, and the dubs end up in different players.
learnMore.solution: One player switches among those cuts. Pick a Language Stream and hear that dub, including a lip-synced version when you generated one.
learnMore.outcome: The player is the same cut the Mixer rendered.

features.title: Collaborate on the cut
features.description: Share one link. Reviewers watch with real playback and leave notes on the picture. You are not exporting a rough file into email to collect feedback.

learnMore.problem: Exporting a rough file into email is how notes get lost and versions fork.
learnMore.solution: Collaborate on the cut shares one link. Reviewers watch with real playback and leave notes on the picture.
learnMore.outcome: Feedback stays on the cut, in the player.

features.title: Release when it is ready
features.description: Publish a 3–5 minute scene, an 8–12 minute chapter, the master, or a promo to YouTube, Facebook, or TikTok, in 16:9 or 9:16, or download the file. Titles, description, and privacy travel with the package. Ship the piece that is finished; keep building the rest.

learnMore.problem: Waiting on the full master delays a scene or a chapter that is already finished.
learnMore.solution: Release when it is ready publishes a 3–5 minute scene, an 8–12 minute chapter, the master, or a promo to YouTube, Facebook, or TikTok, in 16:9 or 9:16, or downloads the file. Titles, description, and privacy travel with the package.
learnMore.outcome: Ship the piece that is finished and keep building the rest.

audiencePaths.prompt: Who are you? Pick your path

automate.label: Automate it
automate.description: Guided workflow — approve pre-vis, ship faster

paths.label: Creator
paths.outcome: Ship on schedule — stop rebuilding in every tool
paths.narrative: You have the story, but every episode means re-exporting assets, re-prompting in new tabs, and hoping continuity holds. SceneFlow connects Series Room, Blueprint Room, and Production Stage in one studio — so you approve the look in pre-vis, generate scene by scene, and ship consistent episodes on schedule instead of rebuilding from scratch.

example.challengeDescription: You have a strong script, but learning six separate generation and edit tools — or getting stuck in slot-machine video loops — slows every upload. Serialized YouTube hits and YouTube TV drama cadences demand faster turnaround than fragmented AI tabs can deliver.
example.solutionDescription: Ship episodic series and scroll-stopping shorts from one studio — beat-first pre-vis, Reference Library continuity, and publish-ready masters for the YouTube-led creator economy.
example.win: Move from occasional uploads to a reliable production cadence with less overhead.

paths.label: In-house team
paths.outcome: Replace slow vendor cycles — control brand and budget
paths.narrative: Internal video requests pile up while agency quotes stretch timelines and brand guidelines drift in every revision round. SceneFlow puts L&D, comms, and product explainers in one guided workflow — your team owns the script, pre-vis, and master output without renting a studio or waiting on vendors.

example.challengeDescription: Comms, L&D, and marketing teams wait weeks for agency or vendor video — or face an overwhelming tool stack with no repeatable in-house system. Every path brings inconsistent branding and stalled campaigns.
example.solutionDescription: Assign staff to produce video on a predictable credit budget — with brand templates, approval before final render, and no crew days or open-ended edit cycles.
example.win: Ship training, comms, and campaign video on your timeline — not the vendor's backlog.

paths.label: Production shop
paths.outcome: Productize a niche with repeatable intake → delivery
paths.narrative: Custom video work is profitable until every client becomes a one-off — new tools, new handoffs, and margins that vanish in rework. SceneFlow turns your niche into a product: repeatable intake, white-label templates, voice-cloned narration, and a clear path from brief to delivered MP4.

example.challengeDescription: Memoir, legacy, real estate, and education clients need fast turnaround — but every project starts from scratch. Per-deliverable handoffs plus slot-machine video re-rolls across script, image, voice, video, music, and edit tools eat margin on volume.
example.solutionDescription: Build repeatable workflows for memoir studios and niche verticals. Template uploads, voice clones, avatars, and pre-vis approval — customize per client and grow margin on volume.
example.win: Launch a video memoir or niche studio service with repeatable delivery — not a one-off freelance grind.

paths.label: Agency
paths.outcome: Faster pitches and scalable client delivery
paths.narrative: Winning the pitch means showing the idea — not describing it — but pre-viz and localization eat the margin before the contract is signed. SceneFlow gets client-ready pre-viz in front of stakeholders fast, then scales delivery across campaigns and 70+ languages without rebuilding the pipeline per account.

example.challengeDescription: Winning the pitch is only half the battle. Recurring client work needs fast turnaround — but per-deliverable handoffs and slot-machine video re-rolls across separate generation and edit tools slow every pitch cycle.
example.solutionDescription: Move from pitch spec to recurring delivery with brand-safe controls, client review before final render, and predictable credit costs per project.
example.win: Deliver faster pitch cycles and recurring client work with less production risk and more margin.

paths.label: Film Production
paths.outcome: Script to an interactive animatic you can screen and test before you shoot
paths.narrative: Previz and audience testing used to mean weeks of storyboards, temp VO, and expensive guesswork before cameras roll. SceneFlow takes your script to an interactive animatic with the Pre-vis Agent — optimize with Audience Resonance, screen it in the Screening Room, and commit budget only when the story lands.

example.challengeTitle: Slow Pre-Vis Before You Can Test the Story
example.challengeDescription: You have a script — but table reads, storyboard cycles, and fragmented previz tools delay investor pitches, audience tests, and greenlight decisions.
example.solutionDescription: Upload your script (MDX, FDX, and other formats), optimize with Audience Resonance, and generate an interactive pre-vis to screen and test — with Production Agents composing prompts and generating across beats, in 70+ language options, and fast multi-language overlays.
example.win: Validate story and audience fit before principal photography — with a shareable animatic, not a weeks-long previz cycle.

solutionPillars.title: Visual & Character Consistency
solutionPillars.friction: Generative models reset with every shot — causing character faces, outfits, and lighting to morph continuously across scene cuts.
solutionPillars.solution: Define master character profiles, environments, and visual styles up front in Blueprint Room. SceneFlow enforces visual identity across every render to preserve narrative immersion.

solutionPillars.title: Narrative Pacing & Scene Control
solutionPillars.friction: Building a film out of disconnected micro-prompts creates choppy pacing, flat emotion, and endless manual timeline editing.
solutionPillars.solution: Direct at the scene level, not the prompt level. Structure dramatic beats, camera movements, and story arcs visually before generating a single frame of video.

solutionPillars.title: Dialogue & Audio Alignment
solutionPillars.friction: Mismatched lip-sync, floating mouth movements, and detached voice tracks immediately pull viewers out of the drama.
solutionPillars.solution: Dynamic voice performance and precise lip-sync are baked directly into the video pipeline — delivering believable dialogue without external post-production passes.

solutionPillars.title: Workflow Friction & Reroll Fatigue
solutionPillars.friction: Generating a short film usually means juggling 200+ raw video files, manual upscaling, and dozens of wasted generations.
solutionPillars.solution: From concept to final master MP4 in one unified platform. Blueprint Room handles story setup, the Writer's Room and Motion sections automate rendering, and Screening Room delivers your final export.

cards.title: Full-Season Animated Series. One Consistent Art Style.
cards.subtitle: Lock character designs, line weights, and shading models across an entire season. Direct comedic timing beat by beat, then review the assembled episode in the Screening Room.

solutionPillars.title: Stylistic Consistency
solutionPillars.friction: Cartoon and anime styles constantly warp between shots, shifting line art, breaking color palettes, and morphing characters into photorealistic uncanny slop.
solutionPillars.solution: Freeze your aesthetic from the first frame. SceneFlow locks character designs, line weights, and shading models across the entire episode so your characters stay uniquely yours.

solutionPillars.title: Exaggerated Animation & Physics
solutionPillars.friction: Generative models struggle with fast slapstick, double-takes, and squishy cartoon physics, turning high-energy gags into melting artifacts.
solutionPillars.solution: Drive dynamic character movement and expressive poses without breaking geometry. Direct punchy physical comedy, sudden cutaways, and wild expressions with full motion control.

solutionPillars.title: Comedic Timing & Rhythm
solutionPillars.friction: Humor lives in the pauses and beat-cuts. Standard 5-second generative loops force awkward pacing that destroys joke delivery.
solutionPillars.solution: Control scene pacing down to the frame. Adjust dramatic pauses, setup-to-punchline timing, and quick reaction shots directly inside the beat-first timeline before final render.

solutionPillars.title: High-Energy Dialogue & Vocal Sync
solutionPillars.friction: Generic AI dialogue feels flat and mechanical, destroying the energy needed for snappy sitcom banter.
solutionPillars.solution: Map vocal delivery directly to energetic facial performance. Dialogue, expressive mouth shapes, and comedic voice tracks match seamlessly for maximum comedic impact.

cards.title: Long-Form Documentaries. Sustained Period Accuracy.
cards.subtitle: Maintain era-specific detail, narrator pacing, and expert-witness continuity across a 40-minute episode or multi-part series. Review the full timeline in the Screening Room before committing to high-res renders.

solutionPillars.title: Era-Specific Visual Accuracy
solutionPillars.friction: Standard generative models routinely bleed modern objects, smartphone screens, or incorrect period clothing into historical re-enactments.
solutionPillars.solution: Set exact temporal parameters — from 1920s film grain to 18th-century wardrobe textures — so every generated scene stays historically authentic.

solutionPillars.title: Archival Cutaways & B-Roll Engine
solutionPillars.friction: Pairing long-form narrator audio with static stock images leads to rapid viewer drop-off during deep dives.
solutionPillars.solution: As your narrator discusses historical facts, SceneFlow automatically generates timed cinematic re-enactments, document overlays, and archival-style cutaways tied directly to the audio transcript.

solutionPillars.title: Interview & Talking-Head Realism
solutionPillars.friction: Generated historians, investigators, or witnesses often look artificial, with floating jaw movements and unnatural eye contact.
solutionPillars.solution: Maintain realistic, trustworthy interview setups with natural micro-expressions, accurate lip-sync, and consistent expert identities across multi-part series.

solutionPillars.title: Episodic Pacing & Narrative Continuity
solutionPillars.friction: Balancing narrator audio, re-enactments, evidence reveals, and tension-building pauses across a 40-minute episode usually takes weeks in traditional NLEs.
solutionPillars.solution: Structure dramatic tension, suspenseful pauses, and evidence reveals visually inside Blueprint Room, delivering a fully assembled master file in one seamless pass.

cards.title: Beyond Dubbing. Fully Localized Productions.
cards.subtitle: Same storyline, two cities: Houston, Texas and São Paulo, Brazil. SceneFlow doesn't just dub the audio — it localizes settings, cultural references, and on-screen text so each audience sees a production made for them.

solutionPillars.title: Cultural Adaptation, Not Translation
solutionPillars.friction: Swapping the audio track leaves every cultural reference, location shot, and on-screen graphic targeting the wrong audience.
solutionPillars.solution: Start a new Blueprint from the original Film Treatment. Adapt settings, character wardrobes, signage, and cultural context in the Blueprint Room before a single frame is rendered.

solutionPillars.title: Parallel Production Pipelines
solutionPillars.friction: Traditional localization is sequential — finish the original, then manually rebuild for each market. Months of delay per region.
solutionPillars.solution: Run multiple localized Blueprints in parallel. Each region gets its own production pipeline sharing the same narrative structure but with fully adapted visuals and dialogue.

solutionPillars.title: Region-Specific Audience Resonance
solutionPillars.friction: Humor, pacing, and emotional beats that land in Houston may fall flat in São Paulo. A single script cannot carry both.
solutionPillars.solution: Audience Resonance analyzes each localized script against regional demographic profiles, flagging cultural mismatches before production begins.

audienceResonance.title: Audience Resonance: build for a culture, not a language code
audienceResonance.description: Subtitles stretch one video’s reach. SceneFlow lets you name the culture, region, and demographic you are making for, score the story against that audience before you render, and then ship either a dubbed master or a separate high-resonance version per audience.
bullets: Define the audience: eight target regions, plus age, gender, education, and community
Describe culture, faith, and values in your own words — SceneFlow reads the signals
Get a resonance score with section-level fixes before you spend on renders
Dub the master, or produce a distinct version tuned to each audience

howWeScore.title: How Audience Resonance works
howWeScore.description: Audience Resonance combines narrative-structure analysis (clarity, pacing, emotional arc) with target-persona fit against the audience you define in Blueprint — not vanity metrics or post-publish retention data. When your audience description carries cultural signals, the analysis adds an authenticity pass over names, dialect, customs, faith, and sensitivities. Recommendations are tied to specific script sections so you can fix issues before agents run video generation.
bullets: Scores Blueprint and script against your stated target audience
Cultural authenticity checks on names, dialect, customs, faith, and sensitivities
Section-level recommendations — not a black-box “trust us” number
Run before heavy render spend, not after publish

preVisEngine.title: Pre-Visualization Engine
preVisEngine.subtitle: Generating a fully voiced, scored, 40-minute Pre-Vis (the industry term: animatic) in 15 minutes is not a workflow step — that is the product. In Hollywood, pre-vis takes weeks and costs hundreds of thousands of dollars. SceneFlow scales it to minutes and pocket change.
preVisEngine.narrative: In the film industry, a storyboard is something you hand to a crew. Pre-vis is what you show studio executives, investors, and producers to get a project greenlit. SceneFlow elevates production from consumer creator tool to enterprise-grade pipeline asset.

pillars.title: The Ultimate Pitch Deck
pillars.description: Upload a script and walk into a pitch meeting with a fully voiced, scored, multi-language pre-vis plus hard data from Audience Resonance. Give creators a data-backed, audio-visual cheat code to get their movies made.

pillars.title: Fail-Fast Pre-Production
pillars.description: Traditional pre-vis requires 3D animators, storyboard artists, and voice actors for weeks. If a scene does not work, tens of thousands of dollars are wasted. Iterate in 15 minutes before a single camera crew member is hired.

pillars.title: Financier Analytics
pillars.description: Audience Resonance at upload appeals to the most risk-averse part of the industry: financiers. Show how pacing, tone, and dialogue align with target demographics before a single dollar is spent on production.

workflow.title: Reference Library → Pre-Vis → Motion Video → ProRes 4K master
steps: Build the Reference Library — characters, locations, and props locked to your production art style.
Generate Pre-Vis shot frames per scene with dialogue, SFX, and music — iterate direction in the Screening Room at low cost.
Approve the Pre-Vis, then generate per-scene motion video with multilanguage dubbing and scene-level edits.
Deliver the ProRes 4K master from the Screening Room — auto-publish to YouTube or download the bundle.
